neighbours.label: 'expression' / 'term' as a syntactic construct of a formal language (grammar <expr>, Expr AST node, lambda-calculus term, syntax-tree expression)
fire: The compiler first turns each expression in the source into a node of the syntax tree.
In combinatory logic, every term is built from the constants S and K by application.
A context-free grammar says how an expression may be rewritten into smaller subexpressions.
In the simply typed lambda calculus, each term is assigned a type by the typing rules.
The interpreter walks the parse tree and evaluates each expression node in turn.
quiet: His expression darkened when he heard the news from the hospital.
Protein expression in the tumour cells was measured after the treatment.
'Spill the beans' is a common English expression meaning to reveal a secret.
The lease has a term of two years and can be renewed by either party.
